title: Gradient Boosted Trees
description: Ensemble technique training trees sequentially to correct prior errors.
name: Gradient Boosted Trees
summary: Gradient Boosted Trees construct trees sequentially, where each new tree is trained to predict the residual errors of the combined ensemble. It optimizes arbitrary differentiable loss functions via gradient descent.
use_when: Working with tabular datasets where achieving state-of-the-art predictive accuracy is the primary goal.
avoid_when: Training resources are limited or high model interpretability is required.
pros: Provides state-of-the-art accuracy on tabular datasets.
Supports custom loss functions and handles missing values natively in modern frameworks.
Can handle complex non-linear relationships and high-dimensional features.
cons: Highly sensitive to hyperparameter choices and prone to overfitting if not regularized.
Requires sequential training, making it slower to train than parallel Random Forests.
Computationally intensive to tune compared to other ensemble methods.

key_hyperparams.name: learning_rate
key_hyperparams.note: Shrinkage parameter to reduce the contribution of each tree. Crucial for tuning.

quick_start:
from sklearn.ensemble import GradientBoostingClassifier
import numpy as np

X = np.random.randn(100, 4)
y = np.random.randint(0, 2, size=100)
clf = GradientBoostingClassifier(n_estimators=100, learning_rate=0.1).fit(X, y)
preds = clf.predict([[0, 0, 0, 0]])
